# Portrait Particles

The `Portrait Particles` asset allows you to create a fun and simple face Lens with particles. The asset features multiple particle presets that you can add behind the user. For further customization, you can also use your own particles.

Find the `Portrait Particles` asset in the Asset Library and import it into your project. Click [here](/lens-studio/assets-pipeline/asset-library/asset-library-overview.md#prefab) to learn more about how to use assets in the Asset Library.

## Import Asset[​**](#import-asset "Copy to clipboard")

Once you import the asset from Asset Library, you can find the package in the Asset Browser.

![](/assets/images/portrait-particles-import-package-d4cfb6f48d1351d6b879256afa0a2420.png)

Follow the instructions.

1. Drag the prefab `Portrait Particles__PLACE_IN_SCENE` into Scene Hierarchy to create a new Scene Object.

[](/img/lens-studio/5-features/portrait-particles-drag-prefab.webm)

2. Attach `Segmentation Texture_ADD_AS_CAMERA_MASK_TEXTURE` to Camera Object Mask Texture field.

[](/img/lens-studio/5-features/portrait-particles-body-segmentation.webm)

You can right-click and select `Unpack for Editing` from the drop-down menu to unpack all assets stored in the bundle. Click here to learn more about [Asset Packages](/lens-studio/features/package-management/asset-packages-introduction.md). Once you unpack the package, you can then edit its content.

![](/assets/images/portrait-particles-unpack-package-061bf4ee5942d0ae5f85213137f72cf8.png)

## Segmentation Texture[​**](#segmentation-texture "Copy to clipboard")

Click on the `Segmentation Texture_ADD_AS_CAMERA_MASK_TEXTURE` in the Asset Browser, and in the Inspector Panel modify parameters in the segmentation texture. Learn more about [Segmentation Texture](/lens-studio/features/ar-tracking/body/segmentation/fullscreen-segmentation.md) and [Mask Texture](/lens-studio/lens-studio-workflow/scene-set-up/camera.md#camera-settings) for camera settings.

## Particles Controller[​**](#particles-controller "Copy to clipboard")

To get started, select the `ParticlesController [EDIT_ME]]` in the `Scene Hierarchy` panel. You can adjust its settings in the `Inspector` panel to customize your Lens.

You can `enable` or `disable` the background particles by toggling the `Particles` checkbox.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

To change the style of the particles, change the selection in the `Particle` dropdown menu.

![](/assets/images/portrait-particles-types-4c63cae9eba762b9688ecede2cdb00d7.png)

You can adjust the active particles by tweaking the `Intensity` slider.

![](/assets/images/portrait-particles-intensity-dd6d283a1db453286bdaf74ae9b7886b.png)

You can adjust each particle minimum and maximum amount with Simple GPU Particles Controller in each particle effect.

To edit the particles’ colors, select and edit the color properties named `Color A` and `Color B.`

![](/assets/images/portrait-particles-colors-ed28febe72cc002d62f53d8e0acc9170.png)

You can adjust the transparency of the particles by tweaking the `Alpha` slider.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Previewing Your Lens[​**](#previewing-your-lens "Copy to clipboard")

You’re now ready to preview your Lens. To preview your lens in Snapchat, follow the [Pairing to Snapchat](/lens-studio/lens-studio-workflow/previewing-your-lens.md) guide.
